body:
I'm still having some trouble understanding why the values in this table make sense:

- "Meaning": it seems to me the meaning of this token is not "Please autofill a 'User-readable identifier for a'...". The meaning is more something like: "Do not autofill anything, but instead use UI that would normally be used to autofill this field, to instead supply information to the WebAuthn API caller"
- "Free-form text, no newlines": I don't think the canonical format of "don't autofill this field" is free-form text.
- "Canonical Format Example": I don't think that "Tim Berners-Lee's phone credential" will ever appear as `inputEl.value`, which is the intention of that column.

In fact, this seems to tie to my above discussion about how this autofill detail token doesn't really fit as an autofill field keyword at all. Instead, it's more like the tokens `shipping`, `billing`, `home`, `work`, `mobile`, `fax`, and `pager`, which are defined inside the "autofill detail tokens" algorithm. (I.e., their `<dfn>`s live there, not in this table.)

body:
I agree 

```html
<input autocomplete="shipping street-address webauthn">
```

is nonsensical but allowed by the update I'm proposing. However, consider for example:

```html
<input autocomplete="section-login mobile tel webauthn">
```

It would not be unreasonable to ask for WebAuthn credentials on the same box a website asks for a phone to sign-in. Same with e.g. `email`. Since I'm not sure where to draw the line and there's no harm to be done by allowing it anywhere, I did so.

And similarly, `autocomplete="new-password webauthn"` might make sense for a sort of "sign in or create an account" flow.
